Turn text into an audio file with a Plivo voice.

Batch text-to-speech is billed per character, so it needs --yes; --dry-run
prints the request and sends nothing. Text is up to 5000 characters, from
--text or --file (- reads stdin).

--format picks the audio: wav (24 kHz), mp3 (44.1 kHz, 128 kbps), mulaw or alaw
(8 kHz telephony, raw), pcm (24 kHz, raw), f32 (24 kHz, raw 32-bit float).
wav-f32, wav-mulaw and wav-alaw are the same audio in a WAV file. Without
--format the --out extension decides (.wav .mp3 .ulaw .alaw .pcm), anything else
is wav, and the f32 and wav-* formats are never guessed from it. --sample-rate
takes 8000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100 or 48000 for wav, pcm, f32 and
wav-f32, and 8000 for the mulaw and alaw formats. --out - writes the audio to
stdout, which is refused on a terminal.

--text-normalization=false reads numbers and dates as written, not as words
(write =false: a space before false does not work).

Usage:
  plivo tts speak [flags]

Examples:
  plivo tts speak --voice r4_ashley --text "Hello from Plivo" --out hello.wav --dry-run
  plivo tts speak --voice r4_ashley --text "Hello from Plivo" --out hello.wav --yes
  plivo tts speak --voice r4_riya --language hi --file msg.txt --out msg.ulaw --yes

Flags:
      --bitrate int          mp3 bitrate in bits per second (default depends on the sample rate)
      --file string          read the text from this file (- for stdin)
      --format string        audio format: wav, pcm, f32, wav-f32, mulaw, alaw, wav-mulaw, wav-alaw or mp3 (default from the --out extension)
  -h, --help                 help for speak
      --language string      language code: auto, en, hi, bn, ta, te, mr, gu, kn (default auto)
      --lexicon string       lexicon_id of a saved lexicon to apply
      --out string           file to write the audio to (- for stdout) (required)
      --pace float           speaking pace, 0.7 to 1.2 (default 1)
      --sample-rate int      sample rate in Hz (default from --format)
      --seed int             repeatable output: the same text, voice and seed give identical audio
      --text string          text to speak, up to 5000 characters
      --text-normalization   read numbers and dates as words; turn it off with --text-normalization=false (default true)
      --voice string         voice_id from plivo tts voices (required)
      --volume float         volume, 0.5 to 2.0 (default 1)

Global Flags:
      --dry-run            preview requests and local changes without sending or writing anything
      --log-level string   log level: debug|info|warn|error|none (default "warn")
      --no-color           disable colored output
  -o, --output string      output format: table|json|jsonl|yaml|csv (default: table for TTY, json otherwise)
      --profile string     named profile from ~/.plivo/config.toml
      --query string       JMESPath filter on the JSON output, e.g. 'data.objects[].call_uuid' (implies -o json)
  -q, --quiet              suppress non-data output
      --schema             describe the command (arguments, flags, output fields) instead of running it
      --show-secrets       show auth tokens and passwords in API responses instead of [REDACTED]
      --timeout duration   request timeout: seconds, or a duration such as 90s or 2m (default 30s)
  -y, --yes                skip confirmation prompts
